skill.name: swiftui-view-refactor

content.value_statement: SwiftUI views can become hard to read when state, dependencies, and helper views drift into inconsistent order. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to refactor views with MV-first structure and Observation-aware state.
actual_capabilities: Reorders SwiftUI view members into a consistent top-to-bottom structure.
Splits large view bodies into computed views or small subviews when appropriate.
Applies MV-first guidance using state, environment, queries, tasks, and change handlers.
Keeps existing view models non-optional when dependencies can initialize them safely.
Reviews Observation usage for root observable objects and explicit state passing.
Groups large-file helpers with private extensions and clear section markers.
limitations: Does not run or compile the Swift project by itself.
Does not infer hidden product requirements beyond supplied SwiftUI files.
Does not replace architecture decisions that require team consensus.
May need project-specific naming conventions or design-system rules.

use_cases.title: Clean Up a Growing View
use_cases.description: Reorganize a long SwiftUI view without changing layout, state flow, or user-visible behavior.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Conventions
use_cases.description: Apply one member order and dependency pattern across files during code review.

use_cases.title: Modernize Observation Usage
use_cases.description: Review existing observable view models and convert avoidable optional state into explicit initialization.

prompt_templates.title: Review One View
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this SwiftUI view for ordering, state placement, and helper structure. Suggest a behavior-preserving refactor first.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Without Behavior Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this SwiftUI file using the skill guidelines. Keep layout, data flow, names, and behavior unchanged unless a change is required.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate View Model Need
prompt_templates.prompt: Decide whether this view needs a view model. Prefer MV patterns, and explain any case where the existing view model should remain.

prompt_templates.title: Modernize a Large Feature View
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this large SwiftUI feature view into clear sections, private helpers, and explicit dependencies. Preserve behavior and summarize each structural change.

output_examples.input: A SwiftUI view with mixed environment values, state, initializer, body, and helper views.
output_examples.output: A reorganized view with environment values first, stored properties next, initializer before body, and helpers below body.

output_examples.input: A long view body with repeated sections and local branching.
output: A shorter body that reads as a high-level layout.
Related helper views grouped below the body.
No intentional changes to layout or business behavior.

output_examples.input: A view with an optional observable view model initialized after appearance.
output_examples.output: A safer initialization plan that passes dependencies through the view initializer and stores the observable model as root state.

best_practices: Provide the complete view file and mention any behavior that must not change.
Ask for a short change summary after refactoring.
Run project tests and previews after applying structural changes.
anti_patterns: Using the skill to introduce view models when the existing SwiftUI view does not need one.
Requesting visual redesigns while also asking for behavior-preserving refactors.
Providing isolated snippets without dependencies, environment values, or related model types.

faq.question: Does this skill create new view models?
faq.answer: It avoids new view models unless the request or existing code clearly requires one.

faq.question: Can it change app behavior?
faq.answer: The default goal is a behavior-preserving refactor. Behavior changes should be requested explicitly.

faq.question: Does it support the Observation framework?
faq.answer: Yes. It gives guidance for root observable state and explicit observable passing.

faq.question: Can it work with SwiftData views?
faq.answer: Yes. It favors SwiftData query patterns over manual fetching when that matches the view.

faq.question: Is it only for large files?
faq.answer: No. It can clean small views, but it has extra guidance for files over about 300 lines.

faq.question: Does it run tests or previews?
faq.answer: No. It provides refactoring guidance, and users should run their project checks afterward.
